walkthroughs.body_html:
Conflict & Tension between East & West 1945-1972 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Conflict & Tension between East & West 1945-1972 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Conflict & Tension between East & West 1945-1972.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How did the Western Allies defeat the Berlin Blockade of 1948-49?
options: By airlifting supplies into the city
By invading East Germany
By abandoning Berlin
By building the Berlin Wall

mcqs.q: What was the cause of the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962?
options: Soviet nuclear missiles placed in Cuba
A US invasion of the USSR
The building of the Berlin Wall
The Korean War

mcqs.q: Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
options: To stop East Germans fleeing to the West
To defend against a Western invasion
To unite Germany
To house refugees

mcqs.q: What happened to the Prague Spring of 1968?
options: It was crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion
It spread freedom across Europe
It ended the Cold War
It was led by the USA

mcqs.q: Did the Cuban Missile Crisis lead to nuclear war?
options: The Cuban Missile Crisis ended in a nuclear exchange.
The crisis ended with the USA invading the Soviet Union.
No — both sides backed down: the USSR removed its missiles from Cuba and the USA secretly agreed to remove missiles from Turkey.
The Hungarian Uprising succeeded in leaving the Soviet bloc.

mcqs.q: Did the West help the Hungarian Uprising of 1956?
options: The Hungarian Uprising succeeded in leaving the Soviet bloc.
The Western Allies built the Berlin Wall.
No — despite encouraging anti-Soviet feeling, the West did not intervene militarily, and the Red Army crushed the revolt.
The USA sent troops to support the Hungarian rebels.
